sentences.context: things that had been there for months and months, like a piece
sentences.simple: Some bits of food had stayed there for many months. One was a piece of old green cheese.
sentences.grammar: ‘had been there for months’ means the food was there for a long time before the moment you look.

sentences.context: The ugliness had grown upon her year by year
sentences.simple: She got more ugly year by year as she got older.
sentences.grammar: ‘had grown’ looks back over her life: the change was finished before the Mrs Twit we see now. ‘year by year’ means one year after another.

sentences.context: She used to tell people that this was because she had warts
sentences.simple: She often told people that she carried a stick because she had warts on her left foot and it hurt to walk.
sentences.grammar: ‘used to + verb’ means she did it again and again in the past. ‘she had warts’ is what she said (she said: ‘I have warts’).

sentences.context: Mr Twit, you see, had been just as clever with the chair
sentences.simple: You see, Mr Twit had been as smart with the chair as he had been with the stick.
sentences.grammar: ‘had been’ looks back at an earlier time; ‘just as smart ... as’ says the two are the same.

sentences.context: Mr Twit had intended to go away and leave her like that
sentences.simple: Mr Twit had planned to go away and leave her like that for two days and nights.
sentences.grammar: ‘had intended to go’ says what he planned earlier, before something new happened.

sentences.context: Mr Twit, who thought he had seen his ugly wife for the last time
sentences.simple: Mr Twit thought he would never see his ugly wife again. He was sitting in the garden with a mug of beer, happy about it.
sentences.grammar: ‘who thought ...’ adds more facts about Mr Twit; ‘had seen’ is earlier than ‘thought’.

sentences.context: walking-stick which she had somehow managed to hang on to all the time
sentences.simple: She had a long walking-stick. In some way she had kept hold of it all the time.
sentences.grammar: ‘which she had ... managed to hang on to’ adds more facts about the stick; ‘had managed’ is earlier than the time she came down.

sentences.context: who had more sense than the others, whispered
sentences.simple: But the fourth little boy had more sense than the others. He whispered to them.
sentences.grammar: ‘who had more sense than the others’ is a who-clause: it gives more facts about the boy.

sentences.context: even if he opens his mouth very wide, it is impossible for him
sentences.simple: He cannot get a spoonful of food into his mouth without leaving some on his hair, even if he opens his mouth very wide.
sentences.grammar: ‘even if’ means ‘it does not matter if’; ‘it is impossible for him to get’ means he cannot get.

sentences.context: But not so the hairy man
sentences.simple: But the hairy man cannot do that.
sentences.grammar: ‘But not so the hairy man’ is short for ‘But it is not so for the hairy man’: we can eat without spreading food, but he cannot.

sentences.context: I can get rid of some of these balloons,’ she said to herself
sentences.simple: If I can let some of these balloons go, I will stop going up and start to come down.
sentences.grammar: ‘If + present verb, will + verb’ talks about something that can really happen.

sentences.context: How would you like it if it was Monkey Pie they made every Wednesday
sentences.simple: Think about it. What if people made Monkey Pie every Wednesday, and all your friends had been boiled up, and I kept on talking about it? Would you like that?
sentences.grammar: ‘How would you like it if ...?’ uses ‘would’ and a past form to ask you to think of something that is not real.

sentences.context: or they will be made into Bird Pie
sentences.simple: Warn them not to sit on that tree. If they do, they will be made into Bird Pie.
sentences.grammar: ‘will be made’ (will be + past form) tells what will happen to the birds. ‘or’ here means ‘if they do not obey the warning’.

sentences.context: What’s more, it had been painted white to look like the ceiling
sentences.simple: The floor had been painted white so that it looked like the ceiling.
sentences.grammar: ‘had been painted’ (had been + past form) says that someone did this earlier, before they came in; ‘to look like’ gives the reason.

sentences.context: no good going to a country and not knowing the language
sentences.simple: There is no use in going to a country if you do not know the language.
sentences.grammar: ‘It’s no good + -ing’ means ‘it is useless to do something’. Here the useless thing is ‘going to a country and not knowing the language’.

sentences.context: go to a barber to have their hairy faces cut
sentences.simple: Do they go to a man who cuts hair, so he can cut the hair on their faces? Or do they cut it themselves, in front of the bathroom mirror, with small scissors?
sentences.grammar: Two questions are joined by or, so you have to hold both of them until the line ends.

sentences.grammar: I shall is an old way to say what must happen later.
